clue.text: Camilla cleared out most of posh jeweller's collection

indicators.note: most rather than all means the final letter is dropped
a room cleared out has its contents removed, leaving only the walls at either end

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name
Boodles is an upmarket British jeweller; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: The Queen Consort has emptied her jewel box, taking most of a smart jeweller's range.
explanation.walkthrough: Boodles is a long-established luxury jewellery firm in Britain, so 'posh jeweller's' is its name with the apostrophe-S read as the S to trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle, as in 'the whole kit and caboodle', means a lot or group of things taken together.

clue.text: Babycino smeared on son's small hands

indicators.note: something smeared is smudged out of its proper shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A child's frothy milk drink has been smeared over a little boy's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like the body part, but here it means crew members; 'small' makes them young ones. A babycino is a cup of frothed milk for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's hand is a sailor, and the youngest serving aboard, running errands for officers, were boys.

clue.text: Sanction Belgium in a more limited way

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: Sanctions on Belgium are being applied more narrowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' reads as a penalty in the surface, but its other sense is approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to give it approval or endorsement, which is what one does on blessing a plan.

clue.text: Member wears woolly hijab regularly in sporting arena

indicators.note: whoever wears something has it around them, so one piece goes inside another
at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of the two words run together
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP turns up at a sports venue in a knitted headscarf.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters run across both words, so the selection does not stop at the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia in ancient Greece hosted the original Games, and the name is used for large exhibition and sports halls such as London's.

clue.text: Mule with leg broken duly skinned, meat for traveller

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: skinning strips off the outside, leaving only the inner letters

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A mule with a broken leg is duly slaughtered and turned into food for someone on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The mule and the leg are shuffled together; the traveller's name ends with the offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemuel Gulliver is the narrator of Swift's Gulliver's Travels, who voyages to Lilliput and other strange lands.

clue.text: Contractions beginning for Susie, father's seconds from impregnating Esther

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter
pa is father, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: the second letter is taken from each of the following words

parts.note: second letter of each word

explanation.surface: A tale of births: Susie goes into labour, and moments after a father gets Esther pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractions' suggests labour pains, fitting the pregnancy story, but the definition is the general sense of muscle spasms.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary tightening of a muscle, which is exactly a muscular contraction.

clue.text: Volkswagen with answer for something red and Italian?

parts.note: the Passat is a Volkswagen car model
A is the usual abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A quiz: name a German car plus a reply to find a red Italian thing, perhaps a Ferrari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red and Italian' with a car in the clue points to a Ferrari; the question mark warns that the definition is a vague description of a food.
explanation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved uncooked tomato purée used in Italian cooking, so it is indeed red and Italian.

clue.text: Youngster doing three times tables after end of class

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter
working through the three-times table multiplies by three

explanation.surface: A schoolchild recites the three-times table once lessons are over.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece comes after the letter from 'class', so it is written second though it is read first.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a young man not yet fully grown, an old-fashioned word for a lad or youth.

clue.text: Dance in the morning to charge muscles up

indicators.note: to charge something is to load or fill it, so one piece is put inside another
in a down clue, going up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
a.m. marks morning hours

explanation.surface: Dancing first thing in the day is a way to power up the muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: The muscles are turned upside down first, then the morning is loaded into them.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance in two-four time, famous from the Rio carnival.

clue.text: One who succeeded in taking Parliamentary seat?

definitions.text: One who succeeded in taking Parliamentary seat?

parts.words: One who succeeded in taking Parliamentary seat?
parts.note: surface reading: a candidate who won an election and became an MP
setter's reading: succeeded means inherited a title, which brought a seat in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Someone who managed to win a seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded' reads as 'won', but it means 'followed a parent into the title'; the seat is in the Lords, not the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Until 1999 those inheriting certain noble titles automatically sat in the House of Lords, a seat gained by succession not election.

clue.text: Powerful through taking charge after revolution

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: by means of, via

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: Someone gained great power by seizing control after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests command in a coup, but it is a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy describes someone muscular and strong, heavily built like an ox.

clue.text: Confusion west of Tripoli as Rommel manoeuvred

indicators.note: troops manoeuvred are moved into new positions, so the letters are rearranged
on a map west is the left, and across clues read left to right, so the opening letter

parts.note: its first letter, the westernmost one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chaos in the desert outside Tripoli as Rommel's Afrika Korps moved about in the Second World War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West of Tripoli' reads as a place in Libya, but it is just the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is literally a violent whirlpool, and figuratively a state of turbulent chaos and turmoil.

clue.text: Part for hooter has taped harmony to listen to

indicators.note: what is listened to is judged on its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to have something taped is British slang for having it worked out; harmony is peace

explanation.surface: A musician has recorded a harmony for the horn part, ready to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn in the band, but it is slang for the nose. 'Has taped' means 'knows', from the British idiom 'to have it taped'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosepiece is the bridge of spectacles or the guard on a helmet, the part that sits over or protects the nose.

clue.text: Dominant peak on Hawaii

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
HA serves as a short form of Hawaii, as in the code of Hawaiian Airlines

explanation.surface: The highest mountain on the Hawaiian islands dominates the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' simply places the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha describes the top-ranking animal in a pack, as in 'alpha male', so it means leading or most powerful.

clue.text: Little sibling rolled ball

indicators.note: rolling something over turns it round, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: bro is a short form of brother

explanation.surface: A small child brother rolled a ball across the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' does not mean younger: it shortens the word for sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere or globe, such as the jewelled ball held by a monarch at a coronation.

clue.text: Alibi involved burning part of a candle, an expert's field

indicators.note: something involved is tangled and complicated, so the letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the wick is the string that is lit

explanation.surface: A forensic specialist examines an alibi built around a burning candle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' reads as 'concerned', as though the alibi rests on the candle, but it signals the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a bailiff's district, bailiwick now means a person's own area of special knowledge or authority.

clue.text: Fancy a sing in calm Sunday morning practice?

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new form

parts.note: taken as written, the little linking word included

explanation.surface: An invitation to a quiet Sunday morning singing rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' between the words is part of the letters to shuffle as well as reading naturally; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglicanism is the faith of the Church of England, whose members attend services and sing hymns on Sunday mornings.

clue.text: Setter's satisfied eating roughly separated pie filling

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so letters go within others
split apart, so the swallowed letters are divided between the two hosts

parts.note: belonging to the setter, who speaks as 'I'
as in a demand that was met
ca. is circa, meaning approximately

explanation.surface: The setter is pleased after eating a rough slice of pie with its filling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The C goes into the first word and the A into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the sweet mixture of dried fruit, suet and spices baked in British mince pies at Christmas.

clue.text: Flash Charlie's back at home all evening

indicators.note: going back runs the letters from right to left

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet, plus the possessive S
someone at home is in
'til late', as an opening-hours sign puts it

explanation.surface: A flashy man named Charlie is back home for the whole night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like the British adjective for showy, but it is the verb: to sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: To scintillate is to give off sparks or glitter, so it matches flash in the sense of emitting light.

clue.text: Professional tried hard after losing the lead

indicators.note: the lead is what goes in front, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: made a great effort

explanation.surface: A professional athlete pushed hard after falling behind in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a race position, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained person has had the formal instruction needed for a job, so is qualified and professional.

clue.text: Snatch of doggerel on gravestone is anon

indicators.note: a snatch is a short fragment, so the letters are a piece lifted from the words

parts.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: A bit of bad verse on a tombstone was written by an unknown author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anon' looks like the abbreviation for anonymous, which suits an epitaph, but it is the old word for soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic word for soon or shortly, and erelong is another old term meaning before much time passes.

clue.text: Intelligence of chap who's not all there

indicators.note: someone not all there is missing a part, so a letter is cut

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: Doubts about the intelligence of a man who is a bit dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all there' is an idiom for dim-witted, which plays against 'intelligence', but it trims the last letter. Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is British informal for information, the same as intelligence in its military sense of gathered facts.

clue.text: Land punch smack in the middle

parts.note: to chin someone is British slang for hitting them on the jaw

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of five

explanation.surface: Land a blow squarely in the centre of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like the verb to deliver a punch, but it is the noun, a country.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country, and land is a common crossword word for a nation or state.

clue.text: Steamed wheat that has no uses beside a brown foodstuff

indicators.note: having none of something means it has been taken away

parts.note: couscous is steamed semolina made from wheat
taken as written
read as US twice, the letters that come out of the grain

explanation.surface: Steamed grain that is useless, served next to something brown to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uses' is read as US twice, the plural of US, and both are removed. The definition swallows the 'a' as well as using it for the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is the brown powder from roasted cacao beans, used as a drink and in baking, so it is a brown foodstuff.

clue.text: Academic group that is keeping vaguely active

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: i.e. is id est, Latin for 'that is'

indicators.note: active means moving about, so these letters will not stay still

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic body that keeps itself loosely busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaguely' looks like an adverb on 'active', but it is the fodder and 'active' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is a group of eight old, elite universities in the north-east United States, Harvard and Yale among them.

clue.text: Men talked about superficial appearance

indicators.note: spoken rather than written, so the sound matters

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: Men were gossiped about for their shallow looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Guys and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward form or semblance, often one assumed to hide the truth.

clue.text: Courier's left right box for customers

indicators.note: the left of a word, as it is written, is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter, at the left
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
the box is slang for television, the tele

explanation.surface: A courier has dropped off the correct package for the shop's customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' and 'right' look like a pair of directions, or 'left' as 'delivered', but one selects a letter and the other is a legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: Clientele is a collective noun for the clients or regular customers of a business.

clue.text: Malign ring around tree

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: wicked, harmful
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A sinister circle has been drawn around a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, putting the ring round the tree, but it turns the whole pair back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean evergreen grown for its small oily fruit.

clue.text: Child given doughnut after first class fighting

indicators.note: coming after means being placed later, so the earlier-read words are written second

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I
a kid is a child
a doughnut is ring-shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A child gets a doughnut treat after the first lesson in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First class' reads as an opening lesson, but it is A1. The definition is a noun: fighting as a martial art.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial art that uses throws and holds to turn an attacker's force against them.

clue.text: Scrap of pink paper that's a case for scrap collectors

indicators.note: a case holds its contents, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: the Financial Times is printed on pink paper
rag-and-bone men collected old rags and junk

explanation.surface: A torn piece of pink newspaper is put forward as evidence for the scrap merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT, the Financial Times, is a British newspaper famous for its salmon-pink pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken-off piece, just as a scrap is a small leftover bit of something.
